"'''Shakedown'''" is a 1987 song recorded by [[Bob Seger]], from the soundtrack of the film ''[[Beverly Hills Cop II]]''. The music was written by [[Harold Faltermeyer]], who also wrote the score for the film, and [[Keith Forsey]], with lyrics by Seger. The song became a number-one hit on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], the [[Cashbox (magazine)|''Cash Box Top 100'']], Seger's only such top mark singles-wise, as well as the [[Hot Mainstream Rock Tracks|Album Rock Tracks]] chart, where it became his second number-one hit, spending four weeks at the top.<ref>{{cite book |title= Top Pop Songs: 1961-2001|last=Whitburn |first=Joel |authorlink=Joel Whitburn |year=2002 |publisher=Record Research |page=218}}</ref>  In Canada, it went to number one as well, topping the ''[[RPM (magazine)|RPM 100]]'' national singles chart.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.collectionscanada.gc.ca/rpm/028020-119.01-e.php?brws_s=1&file_num=nlc008388.0841&type=1&interval=24&PHPSESSID=0augeifhcoektacm7umo2lrl47|title=Collectionscanada.gc.ca}}</ref>

In 1988, "Shakedown" was nominated for both the [[Academy Award for Best Original Song]] and [[Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song]], but it lost both awards to ''[[Dirty Dancing]]''{{'}}s "[[(I've Had) The Time of My Life]]". At the [[60th Academy Awards]], "Shakedown" was performed by [[Little Richard]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Mull |first1=Marison |title=The Oscar Telecast From First to Last |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1988-04-10-ca-1406-story.html |access-date=March 10, 2023 |work=The Los Angeles Times |date=April 10, 1998}}</ref>

"Shakedown" is a 1987 song recorded by Bob Seger, from the soundtrack of the film Beverly Hills Cop II. The music was written by Harold Faltermeyer, who also wrote the score for the film, and Keith Forsey, with lyrics by Seger. The song became a number-one hit on the Billboard Hot 100, the Cash Box Top 100, Seger's only such top mark singles-wise, as well as the Album Rock Tracks chart, where it became his second number-one hit, spending four weeks at the top.  In Canada, it went to number one as well, topping the RPM 100 national singles chart.

In 1988, "Shakedown" was nominated for both the Academy Award for Best Original Song and Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song, but it lost both awards to Dirty Dancing{{'}}s "(I've Had) The Time of My Life". At the 60th Academy Awards, "Shakedown" was performed by Little Richard.

sections.heading: History
sections.wikitext: Initially, Seger's friend and fellow Detroiter [[Glenn Frey]] was the first choice to record "Shakedown", after having a hit with "[[The Heat Is On (Glenn Frey song)|The Heat Is On]]" from ''[[Beverly Hills Cop]]''.  Frey did not like the lyrics and then came down with [[laryngitis]], so the song was given to Seger.  After the song went to number one, Frey called to congratulate Seger, saying "At least we kept the money in Michigan!"<ref>{{cite book |last=Bronson |first=Fred |chapter=672 Shakedown - Bob Seger |title=The Billboard Book of Number One Hits |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PgGqNrqfrsoC&pg=PT681 |page=681 |publisher=Billboard Books |year=2003|isbn=9780823076772 }}</ref>
